name: Charter of the United Nations, Articles 2 and 51
claim: Sovereign equality, peaceful dispute resolution, prohibition of force and self-defence provide foundational legal constraints.
implication: No forced territorial recognition or coercive settlement proposal.

name: OHCHR civilian-protection report: September 2026
claim: At least 328 civilians killed and 2,105 injured in Ukraine during September 2026 (documented minimum).
implication: Prioritize verified civilian protection and warn against undercounting.

name: Reuters: IAEA-facilitated Zaporizhzhia repair truce
confidence: Medium–high; independent repair outcome not established here
claim: Rosatom reported a locally scoped IAEA-mediated truce for power-supply repairs.
implication: Test narrow technical pause models, not a claim of general ceasefire.

name: OSCE support for monitoring a negotiated settlement
claim: OSCE leadership indicated readiness to support implementation monitoring, if authorized.
implication: Explore consent-based monitoring mandates and funding.

name: ICRC: value of neutrality for humanitarian work
claim: Neutral, independent and impartial intermediary activities include repatriation and reconnecting families.
implication: Respect confidentiality; do not publish sensitive cases or impose advocacy roles.

name: World Bank Group support to Ukraine: March 2026
confidence: High for published estimate; projections uncertain
claim: February 2026 RDNA5 estimated nearly US$588 billion in reconstruction needs over the following decade.
implication: Financing designs need audits, prioritization and local ownership.

name: Trystero: official getting started and connection requirements
claim: Both peers must share app ID, room ID, signaling strategy and password; some network pairs need TURN.
implication: Opt-in peer connection with room-code diagnostics and honest TURN fallback.

name: Trystero: signaling strategies
claim: Default Trystero uses public Nostr relays; signaling and data transport are distinct.
implication: Never claim network or relay availability in offline mode.

name: UN General Assembly leadership on sovereignty and ceasefire
claim: UN General Assembly leadership reiterated Ukrainian sovereignty and internationally recognized borders, cessation of hostilities, and the importance of a UN Charter-based negotiated peace.
implication: Settlement proposals must disclose and test compatibility with international law; do not treat territorial coercion as consent.

name: Paris declaration on security guarantees
claim: Ukraine, the US and Coalition of the Willing participants stressed sovereign security and politically/legally binding guarantees to take effect after a ceasefire; pledges remain subject to their legal arrangements.
implication: Security arrangements require named guarantors, domestic authority, clear trigger, verification, and credible breach response.

name: E3 and Ukrainian leaders on negotiation conditions
claim: Leaders called for immediate ceasefire, negotiations beginning from the line of contact without changing borders by force, legally binding security guarantees, and appropriate EU/NATO consent for arrangements involving them.
implication: Distinguish negotiating starting points from territorial recognition; EU and NATO are not bound by external proposals without authorization.

name: OSCE Special Monitoring Mission to Ukraine — closed
claim: The OSCE Special Monitoring Mission to Ukraine ceased operations on 31 March 2022; it is not a presently deployed verification body.
implication: Any new mission needs its own authorization, mandate, security access, budget and compliance design.

name: OSCE: A Peaceful Presence, first five years of SMM
claim: Monitoring missions face mandate, access, safety and technical limitations; implementation mechanisms cannot be assumed from a signature alone.
implication: Specify monitor mandate, access, reporting, incident review, and obstruction outcomes separately.

name: ICRC neutral intermediary — role and consent
claim: ICRC may facilitate family links and exchanges as a neutral intermediary but can only act with agreement of the involved parties.
implication: Never nominate or represent ICRC without its own acceptance and the relevant parties’ agreement.

name: Reuters: Kremlin rejected proposed 60-day ceasefire
claim: Kremlin rejected a proposed short-term 60-day ceasefire tied to Ukrainian elections and emphasized seeking an overall long-term arrangement; not proof about acceptance of other proposals.
implication: Political willingness and acceptable sequencing cannot be deduced from interest in talks.

name: Reuters: Ukraine awaits details of proposed energy ceasefire
claim: Ukrainian president welcomed a proposed energy ceasefire in principle but said details and actual Russian compliance were needed amid continuing attacks.
implication: Announced proposals are not mutually signed or verified restraint agreements.

name: Reuters: Russian non-negotiable security-zone claim
claim: Putin publicly characterized a security zone in Ukrainian border regions as non-negotiable; this is a reported Russian position, not an internationally accepted legal arrangement.
implication: Record incompatibilities and test whether a draft is actually negotiable; do not convert asserted control into legal recognition.

name: Reuters: Kremlin supports Vatican aid initiative for Oleshky
claim: Kremlin said Russia would cooperate with a Vatican-backed humanitarian-aid proposal for Oleshky; this alone is not a verified, agreed and implemented ceasefire.
implication: Potential narrow humanitarian entry point still requires the other parties, independent access and safety guarantees.

name: OSCE Special Monitoring Mission closed
confidence: High for cited institutional description; not a commitment to this project
claim: OSCE SMM closed after its extension failed to secure consensus; cannot simply reactivate it.
implication: A proposed ceasefire sensor/observer arrangement requires new authority and access.

name: IAEA nuclear safety and security in Ukraine
confidence: High for cited institutional description; not a commitment to this project
claim: IAEA Five Concrete Principles and Seven Pillars are safety norms and monitoring frameworks, not unilateral IAEA policing powers.
implication: Consent and effective protective restraint must be organized by the parties; IAEA can assess and report within mandate.

name: ECHR respondent states and Russia temporal jurisdiction
confidence: High for cited institutional description; not a commitment to this project
claim: Russia ceased to be a party to the ECHR on 16 September 2022; the Court retains competence for relevant earlier conduct.
implication: Do not imply a new ECHR guarantee compelling Russia on future incidents.

name: UN General Assembly condemns purported annexations
confidence: High for cited institutional description; not a commitment to this project
claim: UN General Assembly condemned attempted annexation and called for nonrecognition of illegal purported referenda.
implication: A cooling period cannot automatically legitimate an occupied-territory status referendum.

name: UN Security Council Resolution 1272 (East Timor)
confidence: High for cited institutional description; not a commitment to this project
claim: A UN transitional administration was specifically created by a Security Council mandate in East Timor; it is not an automatically available tool in Ukraine.
implication: Any proposal requires a distinct legal basis, Ukrainian assent, and realistic Security Council voting analysis.

name: ENTSO-E Ukraine/Moldova synchronisation
confidence: High for cited institutional description; not a commitment to this project
claim: Ukraine and Moldova synchronised their electricity systems with continental Europe in March 2022.
implication: Proposals should strengthen an existing interconnection, not claim to initiate it.

name: International Mine Action Standard 07.11 land release
confidence: High for cited institutional description; not a commitment to this project
claim: Mine action relies on evidence-based survey, accreditation, quality assurance and national authorization; technology is an aid to accredited clearance.
implication: AI systems cannot autonomously certify farmland safe for public use.

name: IMO maritime safety in Black Sea and Sea of Azov
confidence: High for cited institutional description; not a commitment to this project
claim: IMO warns of serious dangers to civilian vessels; previous UN Black Sea Grain Initiative expired in July 2023.
implication: An AIS feed alone does not render a sea lane safe or establish a maritime ceasefire.

name: ICRC Geneva law for prisoners and other detainees
confidence: High for cited institutional description; not a commitment to this project
claim: Geneva conventions govern treatment and release of prisoners and other protected persons with distinct legal classifications.
implication: Do not collapse POW repatriation, civilian internee release and hostage-related issues into a political swap.

name: International Mine Action Standards index
confidence: High for cited institutional description; not a commitment to this project
claim: Humanitarian survey, clearance and land-release standards distinguish detection claims from certified safe handover.
implication: Use certified independent quality assurance and national release.

name: EU Council: immobilised asset extraordinary revenues and allocation
confidence: High for EU legislation and implementation; future amendments require current review
claim: EU extraordinary revenues are governed by existing legal allocations, including 95% to the Ukraine Loan Cooperation Mechanism and 5% to the European Peace Facility; they are not uncommitted assets available to a new discretionary trust.
implication: A new fund must identify new or reallocated, legally authorized financing; it cannot double count existing earmarked revenue.

name: OSCE Vienna Document 2011: confidence- and security-building measures
confidence: High for framework, current applicability requires review
claim: Vienna Document structures exchanges of military information and confidence-building measures; no new 2026 agreement implied.
implication: Any updated arms-transparency proposal needs explicit state competence, agreed disclosure scope and review of current applicability.

name: UN Integrated Disarmament, Demobilization and Reintegration Standards
confidence: High for framework; no Russia–Ukraine DDR mandate implied
claim: UN DDR standards outline voluntary, rights-sensitive program design, reintegration and protections across mission and non-mission contexts.
implication: Use only as comparative guidance for voluntary reintegration; do not assume imposed state disarmament.

name: UN Ukraine: From Clearance to Outcomes — mine action
confidence: High for methodological guidance; verify precise publication date
claim: Remote sensing and AI support prioritization but must be validated with field evidence and professional judgment.
implication: No autonomous AI clearance or land release; accreditation and human field validation are prerequisites.

name: Reuters: Zaporizhzhia electricity repair truce reported
confidence: Report of a specific temporary repair arrangement; not a general ceasefire
claim: A narrow repair-related truce was reported around restoring electrical supply at Zaporizhzhia.
implication: Use narrow, monitored repair access as a feasibility case rather than claiming a countrywide ceasefire.

name: SIPRI World Military Expenditure 2025
claim: SIPRI estimates 2025 global military spending at $2,887 billion; Russian spending $190 billion and Ukrainian spending $84.1 billion. Figures are not an available peace dividend.
implication: Model fiscal opportunity costs, not a transferable funding pot.

name: Joint Ukraine Rapid Damage and Needs Assessment 5
claim: World Bank, Ukraine, EU and UN estimate nearly $588 billion in ten-year recovery and reconstruction needs as of Dec 31 2025.
implication: Prioritize Ukrainian-led recovery needs and avoid fictitious finance commitments.

name: UNDP Ukraine Local Development Finance Facility
claim: UNDP, Ukrainian Finance Ministry and National Development Institution launched a local development financing facility for priority municipal, energy, environmental and SME investments.
implication: Existing institutional reference for lawful mobilization of locally directed finance; not a PRA partner.

name: World Bank Ukraine Relief, Recovery, Reconstruction and Reform Trust Fund
claim: World Bank URTF channels donor support into Ukraine Government-led recovery priorities, including power, housing, health and agriculture.
implication: Consider established grant/donor channels rather than claiming new disbursement authority.

name: Council of Europe Register of Damage for Ukraine
claim: The register records eligible claims and evidence, including environmental harm; it does not award compensation or make payments.
implication: Separate evidence preservation and adjudicated reparations from discretionary bargaining and asset-release decisions.

name: Council of Europe International Claims Commission status
claim: The Claims Commission is preparatory and not yet an operating compensation payer; its convention has entry-into-force requirements.
implication: Do not imply claims have been adjudicated or reparations paid.

name: UNDP Study: Enhancing Mine Action Finance in Ukraine
claim: Examines sustainability-linked bonds and outcome-based partnerships for safe mine action and environmental/agricultural recovery; not implemented funding commitments.
implication: Outcome funding may be evaluated, but clearance and land release need accredited independent authority.

name: Ukraine DREAM Public Investment Management System
claim: DREAM tracks Ukrainian public investments across planning, financing, contracting and reporting.
implication: Prefer alignment and interoperability with state-led transparency frameworks rather than a replacement ledger.

name: UNDP Ukraine circular debris recovery study
claim: UNDP published a study evaluating market-based recycling and reuse of war-related building debris; materials require hazardous-contamination screening.
implication: Model safe circular construction with mine/asbestos/contaminant safeguards.

name: UNDP Environment for Ukraine Forum
claim: Ukrainian authorities and partners discussed green recovery, ecological policy, and EU environmental alignment.
implication: Tie regenerative projects to Ukrainian policy priorities and review.
